cards.explanation: The answer is that they share everything they own. The text says no one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, “…but they shared everything they owned.” A whole crowd where nobody says "mine" is a miracle on its own, friends. I can't set a plate of cookies down without somebody calling dibs.

The answer is anyone who has need. The money was laid at the apostles' feet “…for distribution to anyone as he had need.” The apostles aren't keeping it. They're a stop on the way to whoever needs it. I think that's how a good cookie box works too, because it's meant to be passed along.

The answer is False. The text says “There were no needy ones among them…” The reason it gives is that those who owned lands or houses would sell their property and bring the proceeds. They laid the money at the apostles' feet for distribution to anyone as he had need (Acts 4:34-35). So the story says there were no needy ones among them.

The answer is Son of Encouragement. Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, is called Barnabas by the apostles, and the text says that means Son of Encouragement. That's a nickname you'd want on your apron, friends. I've been called worse, and mostly by the dust in a junk drawer.

The answer is True. Barnabas sold a field he owned, brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet. That's exactly the kind of giving the believers were doing. Remember this one, friends, because the very next story comes right after it.

The answer is that Ananias keeps back some and brings the rest. The text says he kept back some of the proceeds for himself, but brought a portion and laid it at the apostles' feet. He sold the property, but he didn't bring all of it. It's the story's turning point.

The answer is False. The text says Ananias kept back some of the proceeds with his wife's full knowledge. Sapphira, his wife, knew what he was keeping. Later Peter says she agreed to it too (Acts 5:9).

The answer is the Holy Spirit. Peter, one of the apostles, asks how Satan has filled Ananias's heart "…to lie to the Holy Spirit…" Then he says, "You have not lied to men, but to God!" That tells you, friends, who was really on the receiving end of this lie.

The answer is False. Peter doesn't tell Ananias he had to give all of it. He asks, "Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal?" Nobody was making Ananias hand over every coin. Peter's complaint is that he lied about it.
The answer is that he falls down and dies. The text says that on hearing these words, Ananias fell down and died. This is a heavy part of the story, friends. I think it's one to read slowly.
The answer is fear. The text says great fear came over all who heard what had happened. That's the reaction it gives us. It's a heavy moment, friends, and I think it's best to just let it be heavy.
The answer is True. About three hours later Sapphira came in, "…unaware of what had happened." The young men had already buried Ananias. She walks in knowing none of it.

The answer is that she says yes, that is the price. Peter asks, "is this the price you and your husband got for the land?" and Sapphira answers, "Yes," and says, "that is the price." It's the answer Peter responds to next, friends. His very next words are, "How could you agree to test the Spirit of the Lord?"
The answer is test. Peter says, "How could you agree to test the Spirit of the Lord?" He says "agree" because Sapphira had gone along with it. Her answer to him is what Peter is speaking to.

The answer is beside her husband. The text says the young men came in and, finding her dead, carried her out and buried her beside her husband. It's a quiet, heavy ending for the two of them, friends. The story doesn't add anything more to that moment.
